subject: Ops clearance request: MedSysh private hosting exceptions
messages:
From: Jonathan Price <jonathan.price@medisysh.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medisysh.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Privacy and hosting constraints for Redwood Private pilot

Karthik,

Thanks again for today's walkthrough. We are excited about a private pilot with Redwood but need to confirm a few non-standard requirements up front so our security and procurement teams can green-light the PoC. Summary of must-haves: 

- Data residency: All data must remain in US-East (single region). No cross-region backups during the pilot.
- Audit scope: Quarterly audits with 48 hours notice; on-site/host access limited to named MedSysh auditors only.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys required; keys must not be exportable off-shore.
- Egress: Egress only to a defined set of IP ranges (we will provide).
- Host access: No persistent shell access by Redwood engineers; jumpbox/bastion access allowed for troubleshooting under audit logging.
- Commercial: Given the scope and upfront engineering, request a 20% pilot discount for 6 months and a 90-day trial window.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to the above as a commercial and legal bundle? If not, please outline the exceptions and any approvals required. We need written confirmation to proceed with our procurement review.

Regards,
Jonathan Price
Head of IT Operations, MedSysh Inc.
jonathan.price@medisysh.com
+1 415-555-0187

Attachment: medisysh_must-haves.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jonathan Price <jonathan.price@medisysh.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Privacy and hosting constraints for Redwood Private pilot

Jonathan — appreciate the clear list. I attached a short mutual-action plan and a tracker for the specifics (MAP_v1.xlsx) so we can iterate quickly. High level: we can meet most of the operational asks but a couple items will require legal/deal-desk sign-off (notably the "no persistent shell access" and the requested 20% discount).

Immediate next steps from our side: 
- Legal will propose redlines for audit and access language (cc Marissa).
- I'll open an internal escalation to request commercial flexibility for the pilot pricing and approval for a limited hosting concession.
- Can you confirm the IP ranges and the list of named auditors? That will speed engineering work.

I'll follow up internally and loop you back in once we have proposed language.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.inference.com

Attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Privacy and hosting constraints for Redwood Private pilot — proposed redlines

Karthik / Lauren — I reviewed MedSysh's must-haves and drafted redlines to try and preserve our platform protections while offering a commercially friendly compromise. Key points of the redlines (attached):

- Audit notice: proposer changed 48h -> 72h notice, with audits limited to a defined checklist and a maximum of 1 business day onsite access during the pilot.
- Host access: disallow physical seeding or on-host installation by customer personnel; recommend Bastion/jumpbox approach for customer auditors and require session logging and post-session review.
- KMS: customer-managed keys supported but keys must remain under the customer's KMS with a documented escrow process; we will not export keys off-region.
- Data residency: we can commit to US-East for the pilot but need a time-bound clause: pilot-only residency (reverts to standard cross-region DR after conversion to prod unless otherwise contracted).
- Pricing request: 20% discount exceeds our deal-desk cap. Need Exec sign-off for anything > 15% or for any non-standard SLA concessions.

I've attached the redlines and a proposed SLA excerpt for engineering to review. If the customer will accept the 72h audit notice and bastion constraint we should be able to move forward quickly.

Marissa Cole
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference.com

Attachments: redlines_mutual_action_plan.docx (docx), proposed_sla.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.inference.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.inference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Escalation: Exec approval requested for MedSysh private-hosting exceptions (D-2026-1147)

Team — escalating for executive consideration. Summary and ask: 

1) Customer: MedSysh Inc. (Deal ID: D-2026-1147) — ARR opportunity if PoC converts: $420k ARR.
2) Customer asks: single-region (US-East) residency during 90-day pilot, 48h audit notice, named-auditor host access, CMK (no export), egress-to-specific-IPs, and 20% pilot discount for 6 months.
3) Legal redlines: Marissa proposes 72h audit notice, bastion-only access (with session logging), pilot-only residency clause, and escalation to Exec for any discount >15%.

Why this requires Exec sign-off: 
- Pricing: 20% exceeds deal-desk delegated discount (cap 15%) and materially reduces margin for the expected ARR.
- Operational carveouts: customer wants named-host access and a shorter audit notice than our proposed 72h. These are one-off exceptions to hosting policy for a regulated customer and set a precedent.

Requested decision from Aditya: approve one of the following options so we can respond formally to MedSysh by EOD Friday:
A) Approve legal redlines + 15% pilot discount (no additional SLA concessions).
B) Approve legal redlines + 20% pilot discount for 6 months (requires Exec-level exception and note to finance).
C) Deny discount >15% and require customer to accept bastion-only access / 72h notice; continue commercial discussion.

Supporting materials: MAP_v1.xlsx, redlines_mutual_action_plan.docx, proposed_sla.pdf, HubSpot deal HS-76214.

Please advise a decision and any conditional language. If option B is approved we will require a signed commercial memo and a Finance counter-signature before committing.

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Escalation: Exec approval requested for MedSysh private-hosting exceptions (D-2026-1147)

Karthik — thanks for the clear escalation and for laying out options. After reviewing the revenue potential and legal's recommended guardrails I will approve a limited concession with explicit conditions: 

Decision (approved with conditions):
- Approve option A with a one-time enhancement: allow up to 17.5% pilot discount for 6 months (midpoint between standard cap and customer ask) contingent on Finance sign-off.
- Approve Marissa's operational redlines: 72h audit notice, bastion-only access for auditors, pilot-only residency clause. No physical host access.
- Require an "Exception Memo" drafted by Legal documenting the decision, the exact language for the pilot-only residency and audit constraints, and duration (90 days). The memo must be signed by Finance and Sales leadership before any contractual language is shared.
- Require SOC 2 extension evidence prior to production conversion and an engineering pre-rollout checklist to be completed by our infra team.

Karthik — move forward with the following: draft the customer response offering 17.5% pilot discount, attach the legal exception memo (once ready), and request Finance countersignature. Do not finalize any onboarding steps until the exception memo and signatures are in place.

Aditya Rao
VP, Commercial & GTM, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.inference.com
